summary: Application layout for portals: skip link, header, responsive sidebar (drawer below 1024 px), main area and footer. Does not depend on any router.
whenToUse: Portals, back offices and dashboards with persistent navigation.
whenNotToUse: Simple public pages: use Header + Container + Footer without Sidebar.

props.name: header / sidebar / footer
props.description: Slots; typically Header, Sidebar and Footer.

props.name: isSidebarOpen / defaultSidebarOpen / onSidebarOpenChange
props.description: State of the navigation drawer on compact screens (controlled or uncontrolled).

props.name: mainId / mainProps
props.description: id of the <main> (skip link target) and other props.

props.name: Header: brand, navigation, actions, sticky
props.description: Header slots; inside an AppShell with a Sidebar, the menu button appears below 1024 px.

props.name: Sidebar: sections, currentId, onNavigate, footer
props.description: Link groups (optionally collapsible), current item (aria-current="page"), navigation callback.

props.name: Footer: columns, brand, legal, legalLinks, social, variant
props.description: Link columns, brand, legal text, legal links and social links in the bottom row; “compact” shows a single row. See also the SiteHeader and Footer page.

inherits: HTML attributes of the respective elements (div, header, nav, footer); ref forwarded.

keyboard.action: Opens the navigation drawer on compact screens.
Closes the drawer and returns focus to the menu button.

accessibility: The menu button exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls; the drawer traps focus and can be closed with Esc.
Navigation items are real <a href> links; the current item has aria-current="page".
The <main> has tabIndex=-1 to receive focus from the skip link.
responsive: Below 1024 px the Sidebar becomes a drawer (real mobile navigation) and the Header navigation is hidden when a Sidebar is present.
The breakpoint is exported as APP_SHELL_COMPACT_QUERY.
customization: Client routing: wrap the app in react-aria-components RouterProvider to use the consumer's router.
useAppShell() exposes the state for custom headers.
commonMistakes: Adding a second <main> inside the content.
Handling navigation with onNavigate without href: links must remain openable in a new tab.

examples.name: PortalShell
examples.title: Portal shell
examples.description: Links only update the example's local state.

examples.name: ControlledSidebar
examples.title: Controlled drawer and collapsible sections
examples.description: isSidebarOpen + onSidebarOpenChange, Reports section collapsed on start, a disabled item and a Sidebar footer; useAppShell() shows the button only in the compact layout.

examples.name: WithoutSidebar
examples.title: Public site without Sidebar
examples.description: Header with NavigationMenu and a sign-in action, Footer with link columns.

limits: The switch to a drawer uses matchMedia on the viewport, not the container width.
